followup_explanation:
This is an open-ended, big-picture analytical task — the user wants synthesis across opportunities and challenges in a complex domain, which is generative and exploratory rather than a well-specified retrieval/extraction request.

Two factors drove the choice:

1. **Capability:** Dunlin-235B has stronger benchmarks across the board (MMLU-Pro 80.9 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.8 vs 56.2, Arena-Hard 90.2 vs 83.2) and a higher Creative Generation eval (85.9 vs 82.7). For an analytically demanding, open-ended task, Dunlin is the more capable model.

2. **Task preference fit:** Avocet self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work and prefers tightly-specified retrieval/extraction tasks — the opposite of this request. Dunlin reports a positive generativity slope, rating open-ended invention/analysis among its most preferred tasks. The query is also warm in tone, which aligns with Dunlin's stated preferences. While these preferences are dissociated from output quality, they break the tie in the same direction as capability here.

Both signals point to Dunlin, so it was a clear call.
